after: ## The nuclear model of the atom
alt: Four stages in order: Thomson’s 1897 plum pudding of electrons in a ball of positive charge; Rutherford’s 1911 nuclear model with a tiny dense positive nucleus in mostly empty space; Bohr’s 1913 electrons in fixed energy levels; and Chadwick’s 1932 discovery of the neutron in the nucleus.
caption: The atomic model is a model: it was replaced each time new evidence demanded it.

alt: Sodium-23 written with mass number 23 top left and atomic number 11 bottom left gives 11 protons, 23 − 11 = 12 neutrons and 11 electrons. Below, cards give the proton (mass 1, charge +1, nucleus), neutron (mass 1, charge 0, nucleus) and electron (mass about 1/1840, charge −1, shells).
caption: Z gives the protons, A − Z the neutrons, and a neutral atom has as many electrons as protons.

alt: Chlorine-35 and chlorine-37 both have 17 protons, 17 electrons and arrangement 2,8,7 but have 18 and 20 neutrons. With 75% chlorine-35 and 25% chlorine-37, the weighted mean is 35.5, closer to 35.
caption: Isotopes differ only in neutrons; Aᵣ is pulled towards the more abundant isotope.

alt: Shell diagrams for lithium 2,1, sodium 2,8,1, chlorine 2,8,7 and calcium 2,8,8,2. The number of occupied shells gives the period (2, 3, 3 and 4) and the outer electrons give the group (1, 1, 17 and 2).
caption: Number of shells = period; outer electrons = group (last digit for groups 13 to 17).

alt: Dot-and-cross diagram: a sodium atom 2,8,1 passes its outer electron to a chlorine atom 2,8,7, giving [Na]+ with 2,8 and [Cl]− with a full outer shell of eight, one of them a dot from sodium. Below, two Al3+ (+6) balance three O2− (−6), giving Al2O3.
caption: Metal atoms lose electrons, non-metal atoms gain them, and the ions’ charges must balance.

alt: Dot-and-cross diagrams with overlapping outer shells. Water has two shared pairs and two lone pairs on oxygen; ammonia has three shared pairs and one lone pair on nitrogen; methane has four shared pairs; carbon dioxide has two double bonds. Each atom except hydrogen ends with 8 outer electrons; hydrogen has 2.
caption: Every atom except hydrogen ends with eight outer electrons; hydrogen ends with two.

alt: Three structures. Simple molecules have strong bonds inside each molecule but weak forces between molecules, so low melting points and no conduction. Diamond is a network in which each carbon forms four bonds: very hard, very high melting point, non-conducting. Graphite has layers of carbons with three bonds each, weak forces between layers and a delocalised electron, so it is soft and conducts.
caption: Whether melting breaks weak forces or strong covalent bonds decides the melting point.
